observation.visible_scene: A white ceramic mug with a handle on its left side sits on a plain white surface. Inside the mug, a small red disc-shaped object rests at the bottom, surrounded by clear water. At the very start a transparent plastic bottle is tilted over the mug's rim.
visible_changes: At t=0 the bottle's mouth is at the rim; by t≈0.07 the bottle is lifted upward and a hand holding it appears at the top right with a thin stream of liquid briefly visible, and by t≈0.14 the bottle has left the frame.

After the bottle is gone, the red object stays at the bottom of the water while a small white bubbly patch on its top surface shifts position and size across the wide-shot frames (appearing on the right, then top, then left, then lower edge), then is no longer visible in the later close-up frames.

The framing gradually tightens from about t≈1.5 onward: the mug fills an increasing share of the image, the handle drifts toward and partly off the left edge, and the red object grows larger at the bottom.
The red object's position relative to the mug interior remains roughly centered throughout, indicating the size change is due to camera approach/zoom rather than object movement.
The water surface becomes more discernible as a faint ellipse in the close-up frames.
outside_clip_unknowns: What the red object is and whether it is dissolving or reacting.
Whether the pouring began before this excerpt and what happens after it.
The full action of the hand/operator.
uncertain_details: Whether the white patch is bubbles or a surface feature of the object.
Whether the tightening of the view is a continuous zoom or a cut (no clear seam is visible; it appears continuous).
